nodes.name: Precipitation of Ni-Mo oxide
nodes.procedure: First, an aqueous solution of nickel hexamine and ammonium molybdate was prepared at a 6:4 mol ratio of Ni to Mo. Then the mixture was rapidly heated in diethylene glycol, leading to precipitation of a green mixed Ni-Mo oxide powder. The initial precipitation was also successfully performed with water as the solvent.

nodes.description: HER galvanostatic stability at -20 mA/cm² in alkaline conditions
nodes.source_text: The stability of the deposited Ni-Mo electrocatalyst films was evaluated... Under alkaline conditions, the overpotential at J = -20 mA cm⁻² was stable for 100 h, and in fact η decreased approximately linearly with log(time) over the time period.

Under acidic conditions, the η required to pass -20 mA cm⁻² was also initially <100 mV. However, in acid, η increased (linearly) with log(time), and the performance degraded rapidly after ~7 h under galvanostatic conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Mo oxide and Ni-Mo nanopowders exhibit polydisperse nanoparticulate morphology with particle sizes ranging from 50 to 300 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 shows scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) images of the Ni-Mo oxide and Ni-Mo nanopowders. The Ni-Mo oxide exhibited a polydisperse nanoparticulate morphology, with particle sizes ranging from 50 to 300 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Mo oxide exhibited low crystallinity by electron diffraction. Ni-Mo nanopowder exhibited increased crystallinity and porosity upon reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxide also exhibited low crystallinity by electron diffraction (Supporting Information). Upon reduction, the powder ... exhibited increased crystallinity (Supporting Information) and porosity (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: For powders with ≤40% Mo content, Ni:Mo atomic ratios match precursor solutions; higher Mo precursors result in lower Mo content in catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopic analysis integrated in the SEM indicated that, for powders that had ≤40% Mo content, the Ni:Mo atomic ratios in the powders generally were in accord with the Ni:Mo atomic ratios in the precursor solutions.
